sliding-window-maximum.d: Return the maximum of each window of size k as it slides across the array.
sliding-window-maximum.i: Monotonic deque of indices with decreasing values. Pop from the back while the new value is >= the back; drop the front if it's out of the window. The front is always the window max.

sort-colors.d: Sort an array of 0s, 1s and 2s in place without a library sort.
sort-colors.i: Dutch national flag: pointers low, mid, high. 0 -> swap to low (low++, mid++); 1 -> mid++; 2 -> swap to high (high--, don't advance mid, since the swapped-in value is unchecked).

sort-list.d: Sort a linked list in O(n log n).
sort-list.i: Merge sort: split at the middle with slow/fast (fast starts at head.next so the split is balanced), sort both halves recursively, and merge the two sorted lists.

spiral-matrix.d: Return all elements of a matrix in clockwise spiral order.
spiral-matrix.i: Keep four boundaries (top, bottom, left, right). Traverse the top row, right column, bottom row and left column, shrinking a boundary after each. Re-check top <= bottom and left <= right before the 3rd and 4th legs.

split-linked-list-in-parts.d: Split a linked list into k consecutive parts whose sizes differ by at most 1, with larger parts first (some may be null).
split-linked-list-in-parts.i: Count the length L. Each part gets L/k nodes, and the first L%k parts get one extra. Walk and cut accordingly.
k: Count, then cut sizes L/k (+1 for the first L%k)

sqrtx.d: Return floor(sqrt(x)) without using pow or sqrt.
sqrtx.i: Binary search for the largest m with m*m <= x. Use long for m*m to avoid overflow.

step-by-step-directions-from-a-binary-tr.d: Give the shortest path from node startValue to node destValue as a string of 'L' (left child), 'R' (right child) and 'U' (parent).
step-by-step-directions-from-a-binary-tr.i: Find root->start and root->dest paths as L/R strings (DFS with backtracking). Strip their common prefix (that's the LCA). Answer = 'U' * remaining start path length + remaining dest path.

string-compression.d: Compress a char array in place: each run becomes the char followed by its count (if > 1). Return the new length.
string-compression.i: Read pointer scans runs; write pointer writes the char and then each digit of the count. Writing never overtakes reading.

string-to-integer-atoi.d: Parse a string to a 32-bit int: skip leading spaces, read an optional sign, read digits until a non-digit, and clamp to the int range.
string-to-integer-atoi.i: A careful state walk. Before each result*10 + digit, check against MAX/10 and MIN/10 to clamp without overflowing.

subarray-sum-equals-k.d: Count the contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k (values can be negative).
subarray-sum-equals-k.i: Prefix sums: subarray (i, j] sums to k if prefix[j] - prefix[i] = k. Keep a map of prefix-sum counts (seeded with {0: 1}) and add map[sum - k] at each step. A sliding window fails because of negative numbers.

subsets.d: Return every subset of an array of unique integers.
subsets.i: For each element choose take or skip (2^n leaves). Equivalently, every mask 0..2^n - 1 picks the elements whose bits are set.

subsets-ii.d: Return all distinct subsets when the input may contain duplicates.
subsets-ii.i: Sort first. In the take/skip recursion, when you skip a value, also skip all its duplicates, so the same value isn't excluded in two different ways.
k: Bitmask + sort each subset into a HashSet

subtree-of-another-tree.d: Return whether subRoot appears as an exact subtree of root.
subtree-of-another-tree.i: At every node of root, run isSameTree(node, subRoot). Faster methods: serialise both trees and do substring matching, or hash subtrees.

sudoku-solver.d: Fill a 9x9 Sudoku board in place (exactly one solution exists).
sudoku-solver.i: Backtracking: find the next empty cell, try 1-9 if valid in its row, column and 3x3 box, recurse, and undo on failure. Box cell for i in 0..8: (3*(r/3) + i/3, 3*(c/3) + i%3).

sum-of-all-subset-xor-totals.d: Return the sum of the XOR of every subset.
sum-of-all-subset-xor-totals.i: Enumerate all 2^n masks and XOR the chosen elements. Neat O(n) trick: answer = (OR of all elements) << (n - 1).

sum-of-left-leaves.d: Return the sum of all leaves that are left children.
sum-of-left-leaves.i: DFS passing an isLeft flag; add the value when the node is a leaf and isLeft is true.

surrounded-regions.d: Flip every 'O' region that is fully surrounded by 'X' (doesn't touch the border) to 'X'.
surrounded-regions.ex: inner O's become X; O's connected to the border stay
surrounded-regions.i: Reverse thinking: DFS from every border 'O' and mark it safe. Afterwards, unmarked 'O's are captured (become X) and marked cells go back to 'O'.
k: DFS from border O's, then flip the rest

swim-in-rising-water.d: At time t you can swim through cells with elevation <= t. Return the earliest t to get from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1).
swim-in-rising-water.i: Minimise the maximum elevation along a path: Dijkstra-like search with a min-heap keyed by the max height so far. The first time you pop the target, that's the answer. (Binary search on t + BFS also works.)
k: Min-heap on path max height (modified Dijkstra)

symmetric-tree.d: Return whether a binary tree is a mirror image of itself.
symmetric-tree.i: Compare the left and right subtrees as mirrors: values equal, left.left vs right.right, and left.right vs right.left.

target-sum.d: Put + or - before each number. Count the expressions that evaluate to target.
target-sum.i: Memoise (index, running sum). Algebra trick: if P is the positive set, P = (total + target) / 2, so it becomes 'count subsets with sum P', a 0/1 knapsack.
